memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make gold filigree settings and two braided chains of pure gold, like a rope, and attach the chains to the settings." - Exodus 28:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A small instruction, easily passed over: braided chains of pure gold, made like rope, connecting the settings on the ephod. Gold is soft on its own, but braided into a cord it becomes strong. Several strands twisted together hold what a single strand could not.

The image of a braided cord appears elsewhere in Scripture with exactly this meaning. Ecclesiastes observes that though one may be overpowered, two can defend themselves, and "a cord of three strands is not quickly broken" (Eccl 4:12). Strength comes from being joined, not from standing alone.

Many of us try to hold our faith as a single strand — private, independent, unsupported. It is exhausting, and it breaks more easily than we expect. God's design has always been that His people be braided together: praying for one another, telling the truth to one another, holding one another steady through the seasons when one strand alone would snap. If you are trying to carry your Christian life alone, that is not strength; it is risk. Let yourself be woven in with others. Braided gold holds what a single thread cannot.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I trying to hold my faith alone rather than being braided together with others?
Who could I invite closer so that we strengthen each other?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You never designed me to stand alone. Braid my life together with faithful people who will hold me steady, and help me be that kind of strength for others. Amen.
